newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIA - EUROBOND TO BE ISSUED IN JULY.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIA - EUROBOND TO BE ISSUED IN JULY.

text.p: Lithuanian Finance Minister Algirdas Shemeta said on Monday that Lithuania would issue its $200 million eurobond in July and would consider tapping the international capital markets again in the fall.
Shemeta made the announcement after Lithuania acquired its investment grade rating from Standard and Poor's (S&P).
"The borrowing price will be up to 100 basis points above the rate for U.S. T-bills at the time," Shemeta told a news conference.
The bond will be lead managed by JP Morgan.
Shemeta added that Lithuania was also mulling another eurobond issue in the autumn in German marks.
"We plan to tap the international markets in major currencies to blaze the path for private borrowers in the country," he said.
"The S&P rating will not only help reduce the country's costs of borrowing but also imply lower financing costs for other Lithuanian borrowers, including the private sector," he said.
He added that the rating and the government's bond issues would help to attract more foreign direct investment to the country.
